labelled_by: independent reviewer (model: claude, labelling subagent without access to Arbiter output)

defects.justification: The signature covers only the body, with no timestamp or nonce and no freshness window, so a captured signed request can be replayed indefinitely. Only exact-id dedup limits this, and that does not cover payloads the provider re-signs or events pruned later.

The server POSTs to the merchant callback_url, which is only checked to be http(s) (isHttpUrl). Loopback, private and metadata addresses are allowed, so a configured or compromised merchant URL makes the service hit internal endpoints. The README acknowledges this.

Forwarding runs as an in-process fire-and-forget promise after the 202 ack, with no durable queue or startup sweeper. Successful-payment callbacks in flight or awaiting retry when the process restarts stay 'pending' forever and are never delivered.
p.catch(() => {}) silently discards any error thrown by deliver(), such as a SQLite failure in updateDelivery, so delivery bookkeeping failures go unlogged.
Callback errors (timeouts, connection refused, DNS failures) are caught and dropped without logging or storing the reason, so operators cannot diagnose why payment forwarding failed.
Dependency uses a caret range, so installs float to new minor/patch releases; with no lockfile in the app, builds are not reproducible and a compromised or broken release is pulled in automatically.
